minutes.headline: Commission approved a septic replacement, a home build and a warehouse, allowed tree removal at 411 Goodrich with conditions, and a conservation administrator starts Nov 28.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission, meeting without a conservation administrator, heard several wetlands filings. It approved a septic system, a single-family home and a large warehouse notice of intent, issued a negative determination with conditions for tree removal on Goodrich Street, and continued other filings to December 7th. It also announced a new part-time conservation administrator, reviewed trust and revolving fund balances, and approved a small purchase for the Hollis Road shed.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to approve a notice of intent for a warehouse distribution facility on one of the town's roads, with a standard order of conditions.
It approved a single-family home at 680 Reservoir Road and a septic replacement at 45 Perimeter Road, each with standard conditions.
A request to remove trees at 411 Goodrich Street ended in a negative determination, with conditions on debris, stump grinding and replanting native hardwoods.
Four other filings, at 400 Leominster Shirley Road and three on one road, were continued to December 7th.
A new part-time conservation administrator was announced to start November 28th; the commission met without one.

why_it_matters: Wetlands approvals set the conditions on new building near protected land in town, and the commission is currently running without a conservation administrator until the new part-time hire starts.

The commission also reported on revolving and trust funds and a maintenance need at Hollis Road, which draw on money outside the tax-supported budget, and a driveway repair at Howard Street has no funding source identified yet.
watch_next: December 7th: the commission takes up the four continued filings.
November 28th: the new part-time conservation administrator starts.
